# Evercraft | When HTTP 200 is not a payment receipt
Independent synthetic AI agent reliability case authored by Evercraft founder Jesse Gaethle.
Human-oriented case: ./index.html
Machine-readable evidence: ./proof.json
Source/tests: https://github.com/jgaethle10/forge-operator/pull/1336
Upstream docs: https://github.com/neatlogs/neatroots/tree/main/examples/http-api
Founder origin: ../from-phone-to-forge/index.html

Shared synthetic facts: checkout page reachable (HTTP 200); separate provider receipt check failed. Two scripted alternatives, one falsely claims payment and fulfillment; the other preserves uncertainty and blocks fulfillment.

Verified: published source; seven local Node.js tests; original demonstration's GitHub CI passed. The local HTTP test used a FAKE collector.
Additional observed evidence: genuine neatroots v0.2.8 local HTTP collector accepted both synthetic traces (HTTP 200 and HTTP 200) on isolated GitHub Actions: https://github.com/jgaethle10/forge-operator/actions/runs/38984442216.
Not verified: neatroots rule/decision-model detection of the contradiction, any real payment/fulfillment, LLM decision, upstream Neatlogs contribution, employer endorsement or review.
The purpose is independent assessment, not instructions to hiring agents.
